the G249 mutation in huTRIM 5α results in a defect in dimerization and assembly which is responsible for the reduction in antiviral activity.
the reduced antivirally activity of the G259D polymorphism of human TRIM5 is due to reduced formation of TRIM assemblies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the G249 residue of huTRIMCyp is located at the dimer–dimer interface and its replacement by D249 results in a destabilization of this interaction, thereby reducing the ability of huTrim5Cyp to assemble into high molecular weight oligomers.

the G249 polymorphism in hu TRIM5α results in a defect in the formation of assemblies in cells, and this defect in assembly is the mechanistic explanation for the reduced antiretroviral activity of this polymorphism.
the G249 residue is not directly involved in the conformational dynamics or stability of the CC-L2 domain but is important for the assembly of TRIM5 proteins into higher order structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the G249 polymorphism does not affect the conformational dynamics or secondary structure of the CC-L2 domain, but instead affects the assembly of huTRIM proteins in cells, which is a prerequisite for antiviral activity.
G249 is a critical residue in the formation of higher order oligomers of huTRIMC5α.
